dialogue.content: 相談役のものです、メッセージは届いていますか？
dialogue.English: Hello, this is the client. Is my message getting through?

dialogue.content: こんばんは、届いております。本日はよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good evening, I've received your message. I look forward to our session today.

dialogue.content: はい、よろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Yes, you too.

dialogue.content: こんばんは、相談員です。本日はよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good evening, I'm the counselor. I look forward to our session today.

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Thank you, likewise.

dialogue.content: まず、始めに年齢と性別を教えて頂いてもよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: To start, may I ask your age and gender?

dialogue.content: はい、26歳男です
dialogue.English: Yes, I'm a 26-year-old man.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。本日はどのような相談内容になりますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. What would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: はい、克服してきたつもりなんですが、人と関わっていると嫌われる、怒らせる感覚があってすごく怖いんです
dialogue.English: Yes. I thought I had overcome it, but when I interact with people, I get this feeling that I'll be disliked or make them angry, and it's really scary.

dialogue.content: ずっと直らなくて、相談させていただきました
dialogue.English: It hasn't gone away for a long time, so I decided to seek counseling.

dialogue.content: なるほどですね。確かに人と関わっているとそういう時はありますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. Certainly, when you interact with people, there are times like that, aren't there?

dialogue.content: はい…
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 例えばどういう時にそういう感覚になりますか？
dialogue.English: For example, in what kinds of situations do you get that feeling?

dialogue.content: 一番強い時は、相手が感情的になってる時ですかね
dialogue.English: I feel it most strongly when the other person is being emotional, I suppose.

dialogue.content: 自分に向けた怒りではなくても、怒りを爆発させている人といると、怖くなります
dialogue.English: Even if the anger isn't directed at me, being around someone who is exploding with anger makes me scared.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。確かに怒りをぶつけている人は近くにいるだけで怖いですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. It's true, just being near someone who is lashing out can be frightening, can't it?

dialogue.content: ですね…20歳くらいのころ、職場でそれが強く出て
dialogue.English: Right... When I was around 20, it became a major issue at my workplace,

dialogue.content: それが原因で調子を狂わせて退職したんですが
dialogue.English: It threw me off balance so much that I ended up quitting.

dialogue.content: 未だにそれあるなーって。
dialogue.English: And I realize it's still with me.

dialogue.content: 職場を退職されるほどだったんですね。
dialogue.English: So it was so bad that you had to quit your job.

dialogue.content: そうですね…
dialogue.English: That's right...

dialogue.content: 怒るような人から
dialogue.English: From people who tend to get angry,

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 離れれば解決すると思って、退職したんです。で、実際解決したんですね。
dialogue.English: I thought distancing myself would solve it, so I quit. And for a time, it actually did.

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: フリーで、一人で自宅で働ける環境を作って、すごくいい感じに暮らせてるんですが
dialogue.English: I'm freelancing now, working alone from home, and life is going really well, but...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 未だに、怒ってる人や、「怒ってるかも…？」と感じる人が近くにいると、すっごい怖いんです。目を背けたくなって、言動もしどろもどろになる感じ
dialogue.English: Even now, when someone who's angry—or someone I sense might be angry—is nearby, I get incredibly scared. I want to look away, and my speech and actions become all flustered.

dialogue.content: どうしたもんですかね、汗
dialogue.English: I don't know what to do about it... (laughs nervously)

dialogue.content: なるほど、、、とても難しい問題だと思います。
dialogue.English: I see... I think this is a very difficult issue.

dialogue.content: 一旦整理しますね。
dialogue.English: Let me summarize for a moment.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: ノイさんは怒りを爆発させる人を恐怖に感じ、対象が自分じゃなくても、周りに爆発させていることにも恐怖を感じる。それが原因で前職は退職。現在はフリーで活動されており環境は整えた。ただ、現状は周りの反応に敏感になり目を背けたくなり、自分本来のものを出せなくなる。
dialogue.English: So, you feel terrified of people who explode with anger, even if it's not directed at you, but just at their surroundings. This caused you to leave your previous job. You're now working as a freelancer and have set up a good environment for yourself. However, you're still sensitive to the reactions of others, feel the urge to look away, and find yourself unable to be your true self.

dialogue.content: いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Does that sound right?

dialogue.content: ええ、あ、はい、そうですね
dialogue.English: Um, ah, yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 以前の職場は主に誰が怒りを爆発させていた感じですか？
dialogue.English: At your previous workplace, who was it mainly that would explode with anger?

dialogue.content: うーん。もう、周りの人間全員ですね
dialogue.English: Hmm. It was pretty much everyone around me.

dialogue.content: 全員が全員、互いに影口いいまくってたりしてました、
dialogue.English: Every single person was constantly bad-mouthing each other behind their backs.

dialogue.content: 僕はと言うと、怒りを出したりするのが下手だったから、ずっと聞き役で
dialogue.English: As for me, I was bad at expressing anger, so I was always the one listening.

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 全員の愚痴を聞いてると、ほんと頭おかしくなりそうでした、
dialogue.English: Listening to everyone's complaints, I really felt like I was going to lose my mind.

dialogue.content: それは、とても辛い環境ですよね。耐えられてきたんですね。。。
dialogue.English: That sounds like a very difficult environment. You must have endured a lot.

dialogue.content: でしたね、、あれはもう繰り返したくないです
dialogue.English: It was... I never want to go through that again.

dialogue.content: 逃げられた自分はいっつも褒めてます
dialogue.English: I always praise myself for getting away.

dialogue.content: けど、似た状況に、いや、似た状況でなくても、なんと言うか
dialogue.English: But, in similar situations—or even in situations that aren't similar—how should I put it...

dialogue.content: まんじゅう怖い、みたいな？笑もしかしてあの状況になるかも、と思うとすごい不安になっちゃうんですよね
dialogue.English: It's like I have a phobia of it, you know? (laughs) The thought that 'what if that situation happens again' makes me really anxious.

dialogue.content: どう考えてもそうはならない状況でも。
dialogue.English: Even in situations where there's no way it would happen.

dialogue.content: そうですね。そういう環境というのは辞めて正解だと思います。
dialogue.English: I agree. I think you were right to leave an environment like that.

dialogue.content: 身体が反応しやすいというか、頭の中にこびりついてしまったんですね。。
dialogue.English: It sounds like your body has become reactive, or perhaps that the experience has become ingrained in your mind.

dialogue.content: ですね。。
dialogue.English: Exactly...

dialogue.content: なんと言うか
dialogue.English: How should I put it...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 同じような状況、ほんとに怒りをぶちまけている人には、早々に見切りをつけられるようになったんですね、どれだけ好待遇の仕事をくれても、そう言う人とはつるまない！みたいな
dialogue.English: In similar situations, with people who are genuinely lashing out, I've gotten good at cutting ties with them quickly. Like, no matter how good the job offer is, I won't associate with people like that!

dialogue.content: だから、似たような状況になったらそれはそれで回避できるようになったからいいんです。
dialogue.English: So, if a similar situation arises, I've learned how to avoid it, so that part is fine.

dialogue.content: でも、例えば全然怒ってない人と一緒にいるときに「もしかしたらこの人を怒らせるかも、怒鳴らせるかも」と思うと不安になる感じです。実際にはそんなこと怒ってないのに。
dialogue.English: But, for example, when I'm with someone who isn't angry at all, I start to think, 'What if I make this person angry? What if they yell at me?' and I get anxious. Even though in reality, they're not angry at all.

dialogue.content: この前、すごく優しくしてくれる仕事くれる素敵な人がいるんですけど
dialogue.English: There's this wonderful person who gives me work and is very kind to me,

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: この人に夢の中で「何がやりたいんだよ！！」って怒鳴られる夢見たんですね
dialogue.English: I had a dream that this person yelled at me, "What is it you want to do?!"

dialogue.content: だからこう、そう言う人から距離を取るだけじゃダメなんだなーって…
dialogue.English: So that made me realize that just keeping my distance from those kinds of people isn't enough...

dialogue.content: なるほど、、夢に出るまで。。本来は良い人なのに素直に接することできないのはとても苦しいですね。
dialogue.English: I see... to the point that it's even appearing in your dreams. It must be very painful to be unable to interact genuinely with someone who is actually a good person.

dialogue.content: はい、その人にもぎこちなく接してしまったりして、向こうにも気を使わせたりして…困りますね
dialogue.English: Yes, I end up acting awkwardly around that person, which makes them feel like they have to be careful around me... It's a problem.

dialogue.content: せっかく環境を変えて、やってきているのに、前の職場のことを引きずるのは悔しいですよね。。
dialogue.English: It must be frustrating to still be haunted by your previous workplace, especially after you've gone to all the trouble of changing your environment.

dialogue.content: ぎこちなくなると、どのような感じになるんですか？
dialogue.English: When you say you become awkward, what is that like?

dialogue.content: えーと、ひたすら不自然になっちゃいます。
dialogue.English: Um, I just become completely unnatural.

dialogue.content: なんて言っていいのかわからなくなって、言葉がしどろもどろになって、どうやって席を立てばいいかわからなくなって、動きはおかしくなったりします
dialogue.English: I don't know what to say, my words become jumbled, I don't know how to excuse myself, and my movements become strange.

dialogue.content: 「自然な行動を取ろう」とすればするほど不自然になっていく、って感じ…すみません、伝わりますかね
dialogue.English: The more I try to 'act naturally,' the more unnatural I become... Sorry, does that make sense?

dialogue.content: なるほど、過去のことがあると、なかなか本来のように接するというのは難しいですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. With that past experience, it must be difficult to interact the way you normally would.

dialogue.content: 当時が100%のつらさだとしたら、今はどのくらいに感じますか？
dialogue.English: If the pain back then was at 100%, how much would you say you feel now?

dialogue.content: うーん、普段は20％くらいです。でも、怒らせるかも、と思った瞬間70％くらいまで上がって、って言う感じですかね
dialogue.English: Hmm, normally it's at about 20%. But the moment I think I might be making someone angry, it shoots up to around 70%.

dialogue.content: 100％ではないので顔に出さずにいられるし、「思い過ごしだから落ち着いて…」って自分に言い聞かせてます
dialogue.English: Since it's not 100%, I can keep it from showing on my face, and I tell myself, 'It's just your imagination, calm down...'

dialogue.content: 50も一気に上がると、相当苦しいんじゃないですか？心配です。耐えられているんですね。。
dialogue.English: Jumping 50 points all at once must be incredibly distressing. I'm concerned. You've been enduring that.

dialogue.content: いやーそうですね、今んとこなんとかなってますが
dialogue.English: Well, yes. I've been managing somehow so far, but...

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。苦しいですねー、、
dialogue.English: Thank you. It is painful...

dialogue.content: だから、仕事のチャンスが来ても、「怖くない怖くない！！」って思いながらじゃないと取れないんですよね、そのチャンス
dialogue.English: That's why, even when a work opportunity comes up, I can't take it unless I keep telling myself, 'Don't be scared, don't be scared!'

dialogue.content: 全部思い過ごしだってわかってるんですが、それがずっと無くならなくて怖いですね、
dialogue.English: I know it's all in my head, but the fact that it never goes away is scary.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。それでチャンスを失うのも、フリーで働いてますし自身を責めてしまいますもんね。。。
dialogue.English: I see. And to lose opportunities because of it... since you're a freelancer, you must end up blaming yourself.

dialogue.content: はい、今んとこなんとか頑張れてるんですが
dialogue.English: Yes, I've been managing to push through so far, but...

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: またその状況が来るかも、と思うと怖いですね…
dialogue.English: The thought that that situation might happen again is scary...

dialogue.content: 今はオンラインで在宅業務だからいいけど、もしオフラインに戻って、対面でオフィスとかで働くとなったら
dialogue.English: It's fine now because I work from home online, but if I had to go back to working offline, face-to-face in an office...

dialogue.content: そうですよね。その思いと付き合って行くのは、疲れちゃいますもんね。。。ええ
dialogue.English: I understand. Having to live with that feeling must be exhausting... Yes.

dialogue.content: もうすごい怖いですね、職場にいる間常に70％になりそうになるので
dialogue.English: That would be incredibly scary; I feel like I'd constantly be at 70% while at the workplace.

dialogue.content: はい、
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: うんうん
dialogue.English: Mm-hm.

dialogue.content: 対面だと尚更怖いですよね。。
dialogue.English: It's even scarier in person, isn't it...

dialogue.content: 上がっても40％くらいになってくれればいいんですけどねー…
dialogue.English: I wish it would only go up to about 40% at most...

dialogue.content: そうですよね。コントロールできたら良いですよね。。何点か聞いて良いですか？
dialogue.English: I understand. It would be great if you could control it. May I ask a few questions?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 前職とても辛かったと思います。その状況で、お医者さんに見てもらったり薬を飲んだりしたことはありますか？
dialogue.English: Your previous job must have been very difficult. In that situation, did you ever see a doctor or take any medication?

dialogue.content: 人を男性/女性、年上/年下という形で分類すると、どこが一番接していて強さが出ますか？
dialogue.English: If we classify people by male/female and older/younger, which group makes you feel this most strongly when you interact with them?

dialogue.content: 薬は絶対飲みたくなったので行ってないです、
dialogue.English: I absolutely didn't want to take medication, so I didn't go.

dialogue.content: 男性、年上ですね
dialogue.English: Older men.

dialogue.content: 次に女性、年上
dialogue.English: Next would be older women.

dialogue.content: 教えてくれてありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that.

dialogue.content: ご自身で環境を変えるという選択で対処されたのは素晴らしいことだと思います。
dialogue.English: I think it's wonderful that you took action by choosing to change your environment yourself.

dialogue.content: 年上が怒っているのを見ると、萎縮しますよね。。。
dialogue.English: Seeing an older person angry makes you shrink back, doesn't it...

dialogue.content: そうですね、
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: 暴力を振るわれたことはありますか？
dialogue.English: Have you ever experienced physical violence?

dialogue.content: いや、ないですね、あー、あるけど、暴力があるかないかではないですね…
dialogue.English: No, I haven't... ah, well, I have, but it's not really about whether there was violence or not.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 今まで、お話を聞いてきて、
dialogue.English: Based on what I've heard so far,

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: とても苦しいですよね。環境まで変えられて、それでも身体は反応してしまい。。
dialogue.English: It must be very painful. You've even changed your environment, and yet your body still reacts.

dialogue.content: そうですね…
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 私の意見を伝えても良いですか？
dialogue.English: May I share my opinion?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 今も凄い頑張れられていると伝わってきます。なので、辛い時、不満があるとき、吐き出せるは場所を作って欲しいです。（もちろんここでも大丈夫です）いきなり改善と焦るより、退職して100→70になったように、時間をかけて70→40→20→最後に0にして行くのが望ましいかなと感じました
dialogue.English: I can tell you're still trying very hard. So, I'd like you to create a space where you can vent when you're feeling down or frustrated. (Of course, here is fine too.) Rather than rushing for an immediate improvement, I feel it would be best to take your time, just as you went from 100 to 70 after quitting your job, and gradually go from 70 to 40, to 20, and finally to 0.

dialogue.content: はい、なるほど…ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: Yes, I see... Thank you.

dialogue.content: 仕事に関しては無責任とはいかないでしょうかけど、なんかあるまでは仕事を受託してみて、夜とか合間に不満を言えれば良いかなと思いました。
dialogue.English: Regarding work, and I don't want this to sound irresponsible, but I thought that perhaps you could try accepting jobs, and then find time in the evenings or in between to vent any frustrations.

dialogue.content: いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What do you think?

dialogue.content: たしかに、吐き出すのを意識的にやるのは有効そうですね！いまみたいに
dialogue.English: That's true, consciously making an effort to vent seems like it would be effective! Just like we're doing now.

dialogue.content: ええ、特効薬みたいなもがあれば最高なんですけど、今は焦らずゆっくり進んでいきましょう！ちゃんと吐き出す口があれば大丈夫だと思います。
dialogue.English: Yes, it would be great if there were a magic bullet, but for now, let's take it slow and not rush. I think you'll be okay as long as you have a proper outlet to vent.

dialogue.content: そろそろ相談終了のお時間ですが、本日は相談してみていかがでしたでしょうか？
dialogue.English: It's almost time to end our session. How do you feel after our conversation today?

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます。スッキリした思いです
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you. I feel a great sense of relief.

dialogue.content: 良かったです。本日の相談を終了させて頂きます。
dialogue.English: I'm glad to hear that. We will now conclude today's session.

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much.)

dialogue.content: （ロールプレイを終了させていただきます。）
dialogue.English: (We will now end the role-play.)
